rows.snippet: C. elegans specifically avoids certain strains of Serratia based on their production of the cyclic lipodepsipentapeptide serrawettin W2.
rows.assessment: Pradel et al. 2007, PMID:17267603, PMCID:PMC1892944, scientific Abstract; exact normalized PMC match and native VERIFIED. C. elegans denotes Caenorhabditis elegans. Own Results and actual Figures 1-4 distinguish initial entry followed by leaving Serratia marcescens lawns from absence of attraction. A swrA insertion mutant shows reduced lawn leaving but similar multiday killing; reduced avoidance is not loss of pathogenicity. Purified serrawettin W2 on E. coli OP50 lawns and acute drop-induced reversal are separate assays. The 16-hour bacterial-lawn endpoint, 60-minute supplemented-lawn endpoint and acute reversal are not one exposure. Chemical recognition versus a mechanical surfactant cue remains unresolved, and other bacterial cues can contribute. Serratia swrA is not the similarly named Bacillus motility regulator.

rows.snippet: a specific volatile organic compound, 1‐undecene, produced by the pathogen P. aeruginosa is sensed as an aversive signal by C. elegans.
rows.assessment: Prakash et al. 2021, PMID:34086368, PMCID:PMC8246062, Discussion first paragraph, own-study result; directly matched JATS, PMC and publisher text. Native NOT_IN_ABSTRACT is retained, not relabeled VERIFIED. This is its own experiment, not a citation of Pradel. P. aeruginosa denotes Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Figure 1A-B measures PA14 lawn occupancy over 12 hours. Pure 1-undecene gives negative chemotaxis and omega turns in distinct Figure 2 and Appendix S2 assays. PA14-versus-undA odor choice establishes relative preference, not by itself repulsion or complete loss of bacterial repellence. Peer-review reply page 14 reports reversals but no complete lawn leaving after 1-undecene on OP50; the alternative adjacent-lawn crossing assay is not eviction from an occupied lawn. Roaming or higher mean square displacement alone is not directional avoidance. Recipient sensory genetics is not a microbial causal pathway.

source_assessment: Supports qualified microbial induction of active nematode avoidance: PA14 lawn occupancy decreased over 12 h, with reduced lawn leaving in two odr-3 recipient alleles. Actual Figure 1A-B inspected.
Pure 1-undecene gave negative chemotaxis and omega turns; actual Figure 2B-C and two-plate odor-only Appendix S2A inspected. These are separate from bacterial lawn leaving.
Choice between PA14 and undA odors favored undA; Appendix S2C lacks the identified 1-undecene peak. Relative preference alone does not prove repulsion or complete elimination of bacterial repellence.

Peer-review reply page 14 reports reversals and omega turns but no complete lawn leaving after 1-undecene was adsorbed on OP50. The alternative crossing assay measures lower movement to a treated adjacent lawn, not eviction from an occupied lawn.
First replies added second odr-3 and lim-4 alleles and ASH controls; AWB ablation was unsuccessful. Do not describe all initial reviewer concerns as unanswered or claim a completed AWB ablation.

Revised reviewers 1 and 2 accepted the responses. Reviewer 3 retained immune-specificity concerns; authors added atf-4/hsp-4 and other measurements and the editor accepted the second revision. This is not independent replication or blanket physiological specificity.

Appendix S4E-F measures survival separately. Neither survival differences nor absent reporter changes establish universal nonlethality or intact physiology. No immune-pathway or shared-chemical graph is proposed.

Appendix S1A labels a 22 h incubation then a 2 h, 37 C step and one-hour collection; main Methods describes 22 h followed by one hour at room temperature. Preserve these source-specific descriptions rather than inventing a single harmonized headspace condition.

Higher mean square displacement (S2B) and roaming trajectories do not alone demonstrate movement away from a spatial source. Two-plate chemotaxis and bacterial lawn leaving provide the behavioral endpoint evidence.

This broad capability must remain condition-, recipient- and strain-qualified. Chemical production or gene presence alone cannot establish organism-level repulsion, as the Chai context study illustrates.
